title: Rep. Steven Horsford addresses housing crisis and criticizes Trump-era policies - North Vegas Times
text:
Rep. Steven Horsford, who represents Nevada’s 4th district in the U.S. Congress, used his social media platform on November 19, 2025, to address several policy issues affecting Nevadans and Americans more broadly.
In a post at 20:12 UTC, Horsford raised concerns about the impact of large investors on local communities and referenced his legislative efforts: “Nevadans face a housing crisis fueled by Wall Street as investors hollow our neighborhoods one block at a time. I launched a housing policy platform in May to rein in speculators, and I’m glad to see the state legislature building on that effort with a bill that limits the”.
Later that evening at 21:18 UTC, Horsford criticized policies from the Trump administration, arguing they have negative effects on daily life for residents: “Another day, another way that the Trump administration is harming the American people. Nevadans deserve leaders focused on lowering costs — not policies that make travel, groceries, and everyday life more expensive.#NV04 #LowerTheCost #JobsFirsthttps://t.co/dicYHn5Sdr”.
At 22:06 UTC, Horsford addressed federal regulatory actions and their consequences for state-level protections: “Banning state regulations is federal overreach, especially in the absence of federal protections to keep consumers, workers and the public safe. Instead of accountability, Republicans would rather put you in harm’s way. https://t.co/hN8loG3G18”.
Steven Horsford has served as Nevada’s 4th District representative since 2019 after replacing Ruben Kihuen. Prior to his congressional tenure, he was a member of the Nevada Senate from 2009 to 2013. Born in Las Vegas in 1973 and currently residing there, Horsford graduated from the University of Nevada, Reno with a BA in 2014.
